business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-Precision Lathe Turning of Foldable Hydrophobic Cataract Lenses

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 on Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Prevention; Law No. 254 of 29 October 2020 establishing the Beneficial Owner Registry and reinforcing customer due diligence for legal persons; Executive Decree No. 168 of 7 September 2022 regulating the Beneficial Owner Registry; Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations as amended by Law No. 41 of 19 August 2013; Resolution UAF-DG-01-2017 of the Financial Analysis Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero); and the AML/CFT obligations of the foundation agent under Article 9 of Law No. 23 of 2015.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the Founder’s passport or national identity document and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or municipal registrar in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the origin state; if the origin state is not a Hague Convention party, Panamanian consular legalization applies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Conduct / police clearance for the Founder and proposed Foundation Council members
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or judicial records authority of the origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization in accordance with the origin state practice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement evidencing lawful origin of foundation capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: International bank or depository institution holding the founder’s accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized attestation of the bank signatory followed by Hague Apostille, or SWIFT-standard electronic bank confirmation accepted by the foundation agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Spanish-language foundation charter (Acta de Fundación) and foundation regulations (Reglamento), certified copy for the Public Registry and foreign authorities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the Circuit in Panama and the Public Registry after registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama if the instrument is used abroad; no apostille required for domestic Panamanian filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, Foundation Council members, beneficiaries, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury sanctions, and the domestic Panamanian PEP and UNSC list implementing resolutions. The resident agent and any Panamanian bank must apply enhanced due diligence under Article 18 of Law No. 23 of 2015 when a beneficial owner is a politically exposed person. For a high-risk medical device manufacturing foundation, automated negative news screening, annual re-verification, and a written certification that no sanctioned party has a direct or indirect interest are compulsory. FATF Recommendation 25 requires beneficial ownership availability for foundations; the foundation agent must retain a UBO justification file and submit the mandated information to the Panamanian Beneficial Owner Registry under Law No. 254 of 2020.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Plataforma Electrónica de Reserva de Nombres (electronic name reservation portal available through the official website of the Public Registry of Panama, www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in Spanish or in Latin-script transliteration acceptable to Panamanian civil-law orthography. The foundation name must include the token 'Fundación', 'Fundacion', or 'Foundation'. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered legal person or to a pending reserved name. Foreign brand names are acceptable if transcribed in the Latin alphabet without diacritical ambiguity and accompanied by a Spanish translation for registration purposes. Abbreviated or false transliterations that alter the phonetic or legal identity of the name will be rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Sociedad Anónima, S.A., Ltd., LLC, Ltd. (corporate designation tokens impermissible for a foundation)

Banco, financiera, trust, fiduciaria, seguros, reaseguros, bolsa, valores (banking, trust, insurance, securities and capital markets terms requiring prior authorization from the Superintendency of Banks or Superintendency of Securities, as applicable)
Ministerio, República, Gobierno, Presidencia, or any national, departmental or municipal official denomination without ministerial approval
Hospital, clínica, laboratorio clínico, óptica, or médico-farmacéutica (health-care tokens require pre-authorization from the Ministry of Health (MINSA) before name clearance)
Casino, juegos de azar, apuestas (gaming terms requiring license and authorization from the Gaming Control Board)
Fundación de pensiones, fondo de inversión (pension or investment fund tokens requiring financial sector licensing)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or the appointed resident agent must file a written reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) with the Directorate of Registration of the Public Registry within five business days of the notice date; in the alternative, or if reconsideration is denied, a hierarchical appeal (recurso de apelación) must be lodged with the Director General of the Public Registry within the same five-business-day window. The Director General’s final administrative ruling is subject to judicial review before the Civil Administrative Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice (Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia) within two months. If the original 30-day reservation expires, a new reservation application and fee are required before refiling under the disputed name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as the registered seat of a Private Interest Foundation only when paired with a licensed Panamanian resident agent and a physical registered address capable of receiving official correspondence. Virtual office acceptability for the business of high-precision intraocular acrylic lens manufacturing is conditional: the Ministry of Health (MINSA) medical-device establishment registration and the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) inspections require a physical Panamanian premises, production or licensed subcontractor facility, document custody location, and a stated electronic medical-device record repository. A purely virtual location without a real operational physical presence in Panama will not satisfy MINSA pre-licensing inspection nor qualify for the special high-risk medical-device license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: estimated at 80% within the first 24 months after incorporation. The Ministry of Health performs a mandatory pre-licensing on-site inspection before issuing the medical-device establishment registration, and the Financial Analysis Unit may order unannounced compliance inspections of the foundation agent and the foundation’s principal place of business. Unannounced inspections are probable if the foundation is subject to enhanced due diligence because of its high-risk manufacturing classification and reliance on SWIFT wire and letter-of-credit payment rails.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), as amended by Law 63 of 2016; Articles 5-20 on formation, Article 14 on registered office, and Executive Decree 23 of 1997 implementing regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General de Registro de Personas Jurídicas y Fundaciones (Public Registry of Panama, Legal Persons and Foundations Directorate).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Instrument of Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Private Interest Foundation; however, the Foundation Charter must declare an initial endowment fully subscribed by the founder, customarily set at USD 10,000. No escrow account is required under Panamanian law for a PIF; the endowment is recorded in the foundation's asset registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The founder acknowledges receipt of the initial foundation endowment in the amount of US$10,000, which is fully subscribed, contributed, and recorded as unrestricted foundation capital. (2) The registered office of the foundation is fixed at Calle 52, Panama City, Republic of Panama. (3) The following persons are appointed to the Foundation Council for a one-year term: [President], [Secretary], and [Member], each authorized to act jointly in managing foundation assets for the sole purpose of manufacturing foldable hydrophobic acrylic intraocular lenses. (4) The Council is directed to open corporate bank accounts, pay registry and municipal fees, and complete all environmental and industrial license filings necessary for lawful operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección de Registro de Personas Jurídicas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online name request through the Registro Público's Sede Electrónica or in person at the registry service desk, indicating the proposed name in Spanish transliteration consistent with the foundation's purpose of intraocular lens manufacturing. Upon approval, the name certificate remains valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed name certificate request form
Copy of founder's identification or passport
Description of the foundation's purpose and manufacturing activities
Payment receipt for the name search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, file an alternative name and resubmit; request a written reconsideration accompanied by a memorandum distinguishing the proposed name from the cited registered instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and execution of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (Notaría Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter in Spanish and have the founder execute it before a Panamanian notary. The charter must state the initial endowment, registered office address, the composition of the Foundation Council, and the precise purpose of manufacturing high-precision foldable hydrophobic cataract lenses (ISIC 3250). The notary certifies the founder's legal capacity and the lawful nature of the object.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or cédula of the founder
Name certificate issued by the Registro Público
Statement of initial foundation endowment and source of funds
Foundation Charter draft in Spanish
Proof of registered office address for admissibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises observations, amend and re-execute the charter, ensuring all pages are initialed and the final public instrument is signed anew.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation Charter with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile and Legal Persons Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized public instrument (Escritura Pública) with the relevant registration form and proof of payment at the Public Registry's Single Window. The resulting inscription creates the foundation as a distinct juridical person with full legal capacity.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter (original and two certified copies)
Name certificate
Registration fee receipt
Power of attorney if filing through a legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry files a 'Reparo' (query), respond within the legal deadline with corroborating documents or amend the charter and request re-inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foundation Council governance and officer appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council / Internal governance body (notarized minutes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first meeting of the Foundation Council or record the founder's written resolution to formally accept the initial endowment, adopt the registered office, elect the council chairman, secretary, and protector, and approve the commencement of the intraocular lens manufacturing business. The minutes must be signed and kept in the foundation's corporate book.
required_dossiers: Signed Foundation Council minutes
Letter of acceptance from each appointed officer and protector
Proof of registered office address
Foundation Charter registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any governance omission or defect in the minutes may be cured by a ratifying resolution signed by all council members and filed in the foundation's records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial operating registration and Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Servicios al Comercio
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the 'Aviso de Operación' electronically on MICI's Panama Emprende portal. Attach the foundation's registration certificate, tax identification number (RUC) if already issued, and the proposed physical manufacturing location. This formalizes the industrial activity in Panama and triggers municipal zoning inspection.
required_dossiers: Foundation registration certificate
Completed Aviso de Operación form
RUC or tax identification
Productive investment declaration for the manufacturing line
Certificate of registered address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MICI requests clarifications, submit the missing zoning or industrial activity data through the portal using the 'subsanación' procedure to amend the aviso within ten business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección Nacional de Empresas, together with the municipality of the final establishment.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación de Empresa Industrial and Municipal Industrial Operating Permit (Permiso de Operación Municipal).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III – Full Environmental Impact Study (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental) required for medical device manufacturing involving chemical reagents and cleanroom operations; if annual production is limited and no hazardous effluent streams are generated, a Category II Environmental Diagnostic may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater must comply with COPANIT 35-2000 for discharge into receiving bodies and municipal sewer limits (BOD5 ≤ 100 mg/L; COD ≤ 250 mg/L). VOC emissions from cleaning agents and lathe coolants must be controlled via local extraction ventilation and monitored. Hazardous solid waste, including solvent wipes and polymer offcuts, must be handled by an authorized waste operator under MiAMBIENTE's manifest system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (fire prevention certificate and on-site inspection), structural load inspection from the local municipality (Ingeniería Municipal) for cleanroom equipment installation, and workplace clearance from the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) verifying chemical exposure controls, ergonomic conditions, and occupational safety compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign private interest foundations obtain a Panamanian RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) by appointing a resident agent/legal representative and filing Form DGI-006 with the DGI; tax identification is equivalent to the foundation's RUC; no separate VAT ID is issued beyond the RUC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not maintain a check-the-box election; a foundation may elect to be treated as transparent for local sourcing analysis, but the default is entity-level taxation only on Panamanian-source income; hybrid mismatch rules are limited to general anti-avoidance provisions under the Panamanian Tax Code.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS – Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panamanian Value Added Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis threshold; registration is required upon performance of first taxable transaction in Panama; small taxpayers may use simplified invoicing but remain registered.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) phased by taxpayer category; real-time transmission to DGI's electronic tax portal via REST-API/SOAP; digital seal (Código/Firma Digital) generated by DGI for each invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of moveable goods leave Panamanian territory and are zero-rated when title transfers to a foreign buyer; services are zero-rated if consumed abroad; proof of export supported by customs and shipping documents must be kept by the exporter.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims are clawed back with full ITBMS plus 200% surcharge and interest; criminal liability and 10-year statute of limitations; DGI may both reverse refunds and issue monetary penalties, with director liability under anti-money laundering statutes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama is a fully dollarized jurisdiction with no central bank of issue and no dedicated foreign-exchange administration. The prudential banking regulator is the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); the Banco Nacional de Panamá serves as fiscal agent of the Republic for state collections but exercises no monetary policy, exchange-control, or licensing function.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The US dollar circulates as legal tender by constitutional design; the Panamanian balboa (PAB) is a nominal accounting unit issued only as token coins at a fixed 1:1 parity with USD and not as convertible paper money. Panama maintains no exchange-control law: capital and current account operations are fully convertible, free of prior central-bank authorization, non-resident investment gates, repatriation limits, or surrender ratios. Profit remittance obstacles are fiscal rather than monetary: a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is outside Panamanian income tax on foreign-source commercial earnings, such that beneficiary distributions of trade profits from intraocular-lens exports are not subject to Panamanian dividend withholding; only if the PIF realizes Panamanian-source commercial income within a permanent establishment in Panama does a 10% dividend/advance tax apply, payable in USD to the Dirección General de Ingresos. The practical remittance constraint is correspondent-bank de-risking scrutiny of the PIF structure, resolved through substance documentation and full beneficial-ownership disclosure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Nil. Panama imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement: there is no statutory repatriation timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio (effective 0%), and no obligation to route export receipts through a Panamanian bank. Receipts in USD or any invoiced currency may be retained at any bank worldwide indefinitely. Export records filed with the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (SICEX/DOCS declarations) serve trade statistics, duty-drawback, and territorial-sourcing verification only, with no FX compliance function.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Account with Trade Finance and Commercial LC Desk
International Settlement and Escrow Operating Account
Private Client Operating Account and Capital Escrow Account
Commercial Transactional Account with Trade Facilities
Capital Escrow and Statutory Collection Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Panama has no electronic-money institution (EMI) or payment-bank license class; bank licensing under Decree Law 2 of 2008 requires a physical presence, minimum capital, and SBP authorization. A foreign digital EMI cannot passport into Panama and cannot hold a Panamanian settlement account unless separately licensed as a bank. Feasible workaround: a licensed Panamanian bank's API (banking-as-a-service) integrated as a white-label treasury front-end for the PIF, with no regulatory recognition of the EMI as a paying agent. Cross-border EMI rails (UK/EU/BVI) are viable only as auxiliary collection channels outside Panama's domestic account structure and must not be presented as the primary clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Partially mandatory. SBP due-diligence standards (Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Agreement 008-2015) require positive identification of the founder, Foundation Council members, protector, beneficiaries, and authorized signatories. In practice, Tier-1 banks require at least one natural-person signatory to undertake an in-person KYC interview in Panama before account activation; remote onboarding is available only where the PIF is introduced by a regulated Panamanian resident agent (abogado fiduciario), the beneficial owner passes video-KYC with liveness checks, and all corporate documents are apostilled and certified. Full remote opening for all directors is generally unavailable; the recommended minimum is one in-person signatory plus a standing video-KYC protocol for future council changes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ultimate beneficial ownership through the PIF council and beneficiary layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Panamanian legal opinion (dictamen legal) from the resident agent mapping control; certified transcript of the Foundation Charter (acta constitutiva) and statutes; Registry Certificate from the Registro Público; formal beneficial-ownership statement under Law 23/2015 and Executive Decree 593/2019; apostilled passports and utility bills of founder, council, protector, and beneficiaries; three-month account statements from prior banking relationships.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High_Risk_Special_License classification of medical-device manufacturing (intraocular acrylic lenses) without sanitary or quality credentials.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: MINSA/DIGESA sanitary registration or CE/FDA device listing for the intraocular lens line; ISO 13485 and ISO 9001 certification dossiers; manufacturing or tolling agreement; evidence of appropriate product liability insurance; sterilization and quality-control SOPs; valid export purchase orders from distributors or surgical centers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border supply-chain flows between high-risk corridors (e.g., Asian acrylic monomer suppliers and Latin American distribution counterparties).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial invoices, packing lists, and bills of lading/AWBs; SWIFT MT700 LC records or MT103 remittance evidence; Incoterms 2020 trade contracts; counterparty KYC and negative-media screening results; customs export declarations reconciling shipment value, quantity, and destination against the treasury ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, sanctions-list, or politically exposed person (PEP) alerts on any PIF principal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized PEP and sanctions-list declaration for each principal; World-Check/Thomson Reuters screening report; apostilled police clearance certificates; source-of-wealth statement supported by liquid-asset and contract evidence; three professional reference letters from a licensed banker, certified accountant, and Panamanian fiduciario.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Founder contributions flow by SWIFT MT103 from the settlor's regulated home bank to the PIF's USD account at the Panamanian bank; the USD leg clears via the Panama bank's New York correspondent through Fedwire/CHIPS, followed by domestic ledger posting through Panama's clearing house (Cámara de Compensación). The remittance must state a plain-language purpose 'Aportación de Capital a Fundación de Interés Privado' and reference the Foundation Charter number; the bank maps it to its capital-contribution transfer category and verifies against a sworn source-of-funds statement and Foundation Council resolution. Transactions exceeding the statutory CDD/reporting thresholds (cash above USD 10,000; non-cash above USD 30,000) trigger UAF reports via the SBP platform; a High_Risk_Special_License PIF should pre-file the same documentation to avoid information-request delays. No central-bank declaration, exchange license, or capital-account approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlements for acrylic monomer inputs and finished-lens receivables use three rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 direct international wires for open-account and advance payments, referencing invoice and purchase-order numbers; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600, issued by the Panamanian bank via MT700 and advised/confirmed by the seller's bank via MT710/MT707, with presentation files comprising commercial invoice, clean on-board bill of lading or AWB, packing list, ISO 13485 certificate, and beneficiary certificate; and (3) documentary collections under URC 522 for recurring low-risk counterparties. All disbursements require dual-signatory execution, reconciliation to the approved trade budget, and archival of the full contract file to sustain the AML/tax defense. Cross-border USD settles over the bank's New York correspondent; domestic legs settle in USD with zero currency conversion, preserving the PIF's dollarized treasury.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EUR and USD/CHF foreign-exchange forwards executed with the licensed Panamanian bank (or its offshore investment-banking counterpart) under an ISDA 2002 master agreement, used for European distributor collections and Swiss equipment purchases.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNH, and selectively USD/COP and USD/MXN, hedging CNY-invoiced acrylic monomer purchases and Latin American lens-tender receivables that are not cleared in USD.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR and USD/CNH) aligning purchase-payable and sale-receivable currency mismatches on long-dated supply contracts.
OTC vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars protecting tender-pipeline margins in EUR or Asian currencies without speculative open positions.
No USD/PAB hedging is possible or necessary: Panama's full dollarization makes the balboa a 1:1 nominal-unit coin with no forward or NDF market to hedge.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation Government Fee (Tasa Anual de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) / Ministry of Economy and Finance, paid exclusively through the licensed resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within the first calendar quarter of each year (January 1 - March 31); agents generally require client funding by January 31 to meet internal processing cut-offs.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge on payments made after March 31, additional incremental fines for continued delay, denial of good-standing certificates, blocking of all Registry filings, and administrative strike-off after prolonged non-payment (typically five consecutive years).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Declaration (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final / UBO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Directorate General of Revenues (DGI), Panama UBO Digital Platform, filed via the registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial declaration within 60 working days from inscription; annual updating declaration during the calendar month corresponding to the entity's registration anniversary (Executive Decree 120 of 2023).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of B/. 100 to B/. 10,000 per Law 70 of 2019, denial of certificates of good standing, and suspension of Public Registry procedures until the declaration is regularized.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta) - applicable only where the Foundation realizes Panamanian-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Directorate General of Revenues (DGI) under the Foundation's Tax ID (RUC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed by March 31 for the preceding fiscal year on a calendar-year basis; no return is required when the Foundation derives exclusively extraterritorial income under Panama's territorial tax system.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines of B/. 50 to B/. 1,000, default interest of 1% per month, a 10% surcharge on unpaid tax, and restriction of good-standing certificates for non-compliant entities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Operating License (Aviso de Operación) annual renewal - applicable only if a manufacturing plant or commercial branch operates within Panamanian territory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal Treasury of the district where the manufacturing facility is located (e.g., Alcaldía de Panamá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by April 30, assessed on the preceding year's declared operations (municipal tariff approximating 2% of gross income or the applicable fixed-asset base for manufacturing).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal fines, enforced closure of the production establishment, and possible embargo of assets for non-payment of the operating license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: MINSA-DIGESA Medical Device Establishment Permit and Product Sanitary Registration renewal (Class III intraocular lenses)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Health (MINSA), General Directorate of Food and Drugs (DIGESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Establishment operating permit renewed annually; product sanitary registration renewed every three years with the application submitted at least 60 days before expiry; obligation arises only for lenses placed on the Panamanian market.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Seizure of unregistered medical-device batches, fines per the MINSA health tariff schedule, suspension or revocation of the sanitary registration, and closure of the manufacturing site.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: PIFs are not subject to public audit under Law 25 of 1995; CPA-audited financial statements become mandatory only where Panamanian-source gross income exceeds B/. 2,000,000 per fiscal year, where the DGI imposes an audit as a tax-verification measure, or where the MINSA medical-device license conditions so require. A Foundation with exclusively extraterritorial operations has no statutory audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and adopted in Panama; IFRS for SMEs is available for private interest foundations that are not public-interest entities; the Foundation Council must maintain accounting records sufficient to demonstrate the composition and movement of the Foundation Estate.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Law 70 of 2019 and Executive Decree 120 of 2023 require a confidential annual UBO declaration on the DGI digital platform: initial filing within 60 working days of inscription and an annual confirmation during the registration anniversary month. Any transfer of beneficial rights or change in the Foundation Council that modifies UBO data must be reported within 15 calendar days. The registered agent executes the filing under the digital signature of the council president; non-compliance blocks the issuance of good-standing certificates.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and their rights over the Foundation Estate
Register of Guardians (Protector) and Benefactors, if appointed
Minute Book of Foundation Council resolutions
Transfer ledger reflecting all assignments of foundation rights

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama operates a territorial income tax system: only Panama-source income is taxed at the 25% statutory corporate rate. Effective tax reliefs include: (i) full exemption for foreign-source income earned by a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) not engaged in Panama commercial or industrial activity (Ley 25 de 1995, Art. 8); (ii) 0% income tax under the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime (Ley 41 de 2007, Decreto Ejecutivo 38 de 2013) for licensed regional headquarters; (iii) 0% tax on manufacturing, trading, and logistics profits earned within the Colon Free Zone, Panama Pacifico Special Economic Zone, and other free-zone regimes (Ley 32 de 2011); (iv) the mandatory 'Tasa Efectiva Mínima' (minimum effective tax) of 25% applied on the positive difference between net taxable income and 50% of gross taxable income, effectively 12.5% of gross taxable income for large taxpayers (Ley 48 de 2016), which bounds aggressive deduction stacking; and (v) accelerated depreciation and reinvestment credits for qualifying Panamanian manufacturing operations under Ley 41 de 1999 and Ley 76 de 2019. An intraocular acrylic lens manufacturer resident in Panama with a PIF as IP holder may achieve an aggregate effective rate below 25% only through free-zone or SEM structures; a passive PIF earning royalty income from foreign licensing remains exempt, while a PIF deriving Panama-source royalty income is taxable as a commercial foundation at 25%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 202 (Declaración Anual de Renta – Personas Jurídicas / legal entities income tax return), filed exclusively via the DGI 'Oficina Virtual' electronic portal at https://etax.dgi.gob.pa (e-Tax 2.0 system). Advance payments are filed on Formulario 425 (Pago Directo de Impuesto Estimado) for the March, June, September, and December installments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, with quarterly advance income tax payments (Formulario 425) due in March, June, September, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year taxpayers the deadline is 31 March. A two-month extension is available upon prior electronic request through the Oficina Virtual (Formulario 202-P / Solicitud de Prórroga). Non-calendar fiscal years follow the same three-month rule measured from the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered taxpayer number (Registro Único de Contribuyente) and validation digit for the legal entity or permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF or manufacturer without a Panama permanent establishment and without Panama-source income must not file Formulario 202; it should obtain a RUC only when conducting taxable Panama-source activities or maintaining a branch in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Renglón 1 – Ingresos brutos de fuente panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from Panama-source operations, including sales of foldable hydrophobic intraocular acrylic lenses delivered, installed, or invoiced in Panama, less returns and discounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must report only Panama-source revenue; foreign-source manufacturing sales routed through an offshore entity are excluded under territoriality and may be supported by a schedule of foreign income and an affidavit of non-residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from foreign markets and export sales outside Panama, includable for informational purposes only.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF holding the acrylic-lens patent that licenses it to third parties abroad reports the licensing fees in a separate exempt-income line; if the licensee exploits the IP in Panama, the income becomes Panama-source and is taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Renglón 89 – Rentas exentas y no gravables
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt or non-taxable income lines, including passive investment income of non-commercial PIFs, SEM income, and free-zone manufacturing profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the foundation resolution confirming non-commercial status, the SEM license, or free-zone operating certificate; failure to attach supporting documentation exposes the exemption to recharacterization as taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Renglón 210 – Deducciones y gastos relacionados con renglón 1
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, royalties paid to related parties, depreciation of lens-turning equipment, salaries, and deductible operational expenses allocable to Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only if proportional to Panama-source revenue and supported by withholding certificates; cross-border royalty deductions require transfer pricing documentation when the related-party threshold is met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cálculo – Impuesto de Tasa Efectiva Mínima (método DIF)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the minimum effective tax: 25% of the positive difference between net taxable income and 50% of gross taxable income, payable where it exceeds the ordinary tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This minimum regime applies only to Panama-source gross income of taxpayers whose taxable gross revenue exceeds B/.1,500,000; SEM and free-zone taxpayers and non-residents without a Panama PE are outside its scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Renglón E – Impuesto complementario sobre dividendos (10%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional 10% corporate-level dividend tax on profits distributed to shareholders or PIF beneficiaries, payable when the dividend is declared or paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The payer must reduce withholding to the applicable treaty rate only against a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) on file; otherwise the full 10% (or 20% on non-taxed profits) is withheld.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Formulario 202 triggers a 10% surcharge on the tax due if filed within 90 days of the deadline and 20% if filed later, plus default interest at 1% per month on the outstanding tax (Código Fiscal Art. 1071). Non-filing is punishable by formal fines of B/.500 to B/.5,000 per infraction, administrative closure of the commercial establishment, and loss of the deduction for the offending year. Failure to submit Formulario 425 advance installments triggers recalculation of the estimated tax, a 10% recargo, monthly interest, and public registry annotation of the debt. FALSE data carries a 100% fraud surcharge and, where the omission exceeds B/.100,000, criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends or profit distributions paid out of Panama-source taxable profits, withheld by the paying entity (Código Fiscal Arts. 733-735); 5% for entities under the small-taxpayer regime (gross income below B/.1,500,000); 20% on distributions sourced from exempt Panama income or foreign-source income that was never subject to Panama tax, including distributions of a PIF's passive foreign income if recharacterized as a dividend. Dividends distributed by a genuinely non-commercial PIF to beneficiaries under the foundation deed are structurally treated as gift-like distributions and not as taxable dividends, provided no Panama-source commercial activity exists.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Taxation Agreement (Panama maintains DTAs with Mexico, Singapore, South Korea, UAE, Qatar, Barbados, the Netherlands, and related TIEAs), the beneficial owner must: (i) submit an original or certified Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the counterpart tax authority; (ii) file with the Panama DGI the 'Solicitud de Reducción de Retención' through the Oficina Virtual attaching the TRC, beneficial-ownership declaration, and the underlying contract; (iii) obtain the DGI resolution approving the reduced rate before the payment date; and (iv) present the approved resolution to the payer. Where the reduced rate is only granted after payment, a refund claim must be filed within the ordinary prescription period (three years). Failure to possess the TRC at the time of distribution compels the payer to apply the statutory 10% or 20% rate with no retroactive adjustment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid by a Panama-resident debtor to a non-resident lender is generally outside Panama's territorial tax net (0% withholding), provided the lender does not carry on business through a Panama permanent establishment. Royalty payments to non-residents for the use of industrial, commercial, or scientific intellectual property (including intraocular-lens patents, designs, and know-how) inside Panama carry a statutory withholding rate of 12.5%; technical assistance and other intangible services are withheld at 15%. Under DTAs the rates are typically reduced to between 0% and 10% (e.g., Mexico and South Korea DTAs cap royalties at 10%, UAE at 0%-10%), conditional on the TRC and substance tests. Panama does not apply withholding to royalties for foreign exploitation of IP, so a PIF licensing lens technology entirely outside Panama receives the fees free of Panama tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama-source Balboa (B/.) threshold: a taxpayer is mandatorily required to file Formulario 706 (Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia) and prepare contemporaneous Transfer Pricing documentation (Local File) where annual gross revenue equals or exceeds B/.10,000,000, or where transactions with related parties, including a PIF IP holder, equal or exceed B/.3,000,000 in a fiscal year. A Master File is required where the multinational group's consolidated gross revenue reaches USD 50,000,000, and a Country-by-Country Report is due where the group consolidates USD 850,000,000 or more, filed through the DGI's electronic portal within 12 months after fiscal year-end. The thresholds derive from Ley 23 de 2010 and Decreto Ejecutivo 194 de 2011.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Precio Comparable no Controlado / Comparable Uncontrolled Price)
TNMM (Método del Margen Neto de la Transacción / Transactional Net Margin Method)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations, introduced by Ley 70 de 2019 and Decreto Ejecutivo 163 de 2020 (effective for fiscal years beginning 1 January 2020), require every Panama legal entity carrying on a 'relevant activity' - including distribution and logistics, financing, headquarters services, shipping, and intellectual-property holding and licensing - to maintain and annually report economic substance in Panama. A PIF that holds the intraocular acrylic lens IP and receives royalties or that licenses manufacturing rights must demonstrate physical presence, full-time local employees, payroll and premises expenditure proportionate to the income, and strategic board decisions taken in Panama, and must file the annual ESR information return through the SEMS portal of the Dirección General de Ingresos. Passive PIFs without a relevant activity are outside the ESR filing obligation but remain within doorstep concerns; a non-compliant entity faces an annual fine of B/.75,000 to B/.1,000,000, loss of tax residence certification, and the nullification of treaty benefits and transfer-pricing deductions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of Panama-source sales of intraocular acrylic lenses; invoicing Panamanian hospitals through the Dubai PIF to shift revenue abroad; deducting fictitious royalty expenses to the PIF without IP registration or substance; destroying accounting records; using bearer-share style foundation anonymity to conceal taxable manufacturing profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Compulsory redefinition of income, 100% fraud surcharge on the omitted tax, monthly interest at 1%, closure of the commercial establishment, and criminal prosecution under Código Fiscal Arts. 748-749 and Ley 20 de 2013 with fines of up to triple the evaded tax and imprisonment for the responsible officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, foundation council members, and the resident agent are jointly liable for the evaded tax through the doctrine of levantamiento del velo corporativo (piercing the corporate veil); individual assets may be seized, travel bans issued by the DGI and the Public Registry, and jail terms of 2 to 5 years imposed where the evasion exceeds B/.100,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a PIF that books royalty or financing income without any physical office, employees, bank account, or board meetings in Panama; registering the PIF solely to disguise ownership of the lens-tooling assets and patent; failing to file the ESR annual declaration while performing IP-related activity; filing a false nil return despite commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR violation fines of B/.75,000 to B/.1,000,000 per fiscal year, administrative dissolution of the foundation, cancellation of the tax residence certificate, denial of DTA relief, and listing on the DGI's non-compliant taxpayer registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and the resident agent are personally liable for ESR fines, can be struck from the Registry of Resident Agents, barred from acting in Panama for 12 months, and the council member who signed the false substance declaration faces perjury and fraud penalties, non-bailable arrest, and confiscation of personal property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF and Swift-wire payment rails to receive settlement proceeds for lens sales routed through sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions; layering payments to shell beneficiaries; receiving funds from distributors subject to OFAC designation; structuring cash deposits of medical-device sales to evade the B/.10,000 reporting threshold; failing to maintain the beneficial-ownership register of the foundation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines from B/.100,000 up to five times the laundered amounts, freezing of the foundation's bank accounts by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF), suspension of the resident agent's license, and criminal prosecution for money laundering under Ley 23 de 2015 with penalties of up to 10 years' imprisonment and asset forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and foundation council members are exposed to criminal money-laundering prosecution with prison terms up to 10 years, personal asset forfeiture, travel bans, and publication of their names in the UAF register; the professional resident agent who onboarded the structure without KYC faces license revocation and civil restitution to defrauded creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying 'royalties' of 18%-25% of net revenue to a related PIF for acrylic-lens IP while the PIF holds no registered patent, performs no R&D, and has zero employees; failing to file Formulario 706 when the B/.3,000,000 transaction threshold is met; refusing to produce contemporaneous CUP or TNMM analyses within 30 days of DGI request; omitting the CbC report for a group of USD 850M+.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI recharacterization of the transaction at arm's length, disallowance of the excess royalty deduction, 25% tax on the adjusted profit, 1% monthly interest, application of the 100% fraud penalty for false documentation, and late-filing penalties on Formulario 706 of B/.100 per day up to B/.10,000; repeated defaults trigger criminal tax-evasion charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director certifying false transfer-pricing documentation is liable for perjury and civil restitution of the adjusted tax, interest, and penalties out of personal assets; the DGI may impose an exit ban preventing the director from leaving Panama until the assessment is secured by bond or payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing retained Panama-source manufacturing profits to PIF beneficiaries without withholding the 10% dividend tax; disguising distributions as 'loans' booked in the PIF's ledger without repayment terms or commercial interest; charging luxury personal expenses of the beneficial owner to foundation accounts; moving profits to the Dubai PIF and then paying personal expenses without corporate resolutions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of the transfer as a dividend or compensation, withholding of 20% on the amount paid out of non-taxed profits, a 100% fraud surcharge, monthly arrears interest, and criminal liability for the officer who executed the unauthorized distribution; the DGI may also reverse the foundation's exemption status retroactively.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficiaries and the foundation council are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid dividend tax plus surcharges; personal bank accounts and real estate may be attached, travel prohibitions enforced, and directors who voted the unlawful distribution face jail terms of up to 4 years for abuse of the foundation form (Código Fiscal and Ley 25 de 1995 combined reading).
